fixes.explanation: I can see why you'd think so, since Jeremiah brings them into the house of the LORD. But the text names Jaazaniah, his brothers and all his sons, the entire house of the Rechabites (Jeremiah 35:3). Priests and Levites aren't named there. Right building, but that's not who the verse lists.

Home is a natural guess, since in a minute we learn they live in tents (Jeremiah 35:7). Jonadab's command was, "Neither you nor your descendants are ever to drink wine." (Jeremiah 35:6). No at-home exception. Not at home, not anywhere.
Towns is a fair guess, but that's not the word. Jonadab said they were never to build a house, and then, "…you must live in tents all your lives…" (Jeremiah 35:7). So the blank is tents.

True, baker. The Rechabites say, "…we have not drunk wine all our lives—neither we nor our wives nor our sons and daughters." (Jeremiah 35:8). The whole family, all their lives. That's a whole household keeping one rule.

Yes, baker. They said, "Come, let us go into Jerusalem to escape the armies of the Chaldeans and the Arameans." (Jeremiah 35:11). So the Rechabites went into Jerusalem to escape the armies. That's the reason they gave.

Settling down doesn't match what they say. Jonadab told them not to build a house or sow seed or plant a vineyard, and they say, "…we have lived in tents…" (Jeremiah 35:7, 10). The reason they came was, "…to escape the armies of the Chaldeans and the Arameans." (Jeremiah 35:11). They stayed in Jerusalem, but nothing here says they settled.

The text doesn't say that, baker. God says, "The words of Jonadab son of Rechab have been carried out." (Jeremiah 35:14). He adds that Jonadab's sons have not drunk wine to this very day. Carried out is the word, not too hard.

Forgotten would be the opposite of what God says. He says, "The words of Jonadab son of Rechab have been carried out." (Jeremiah 35:14). He adds that the sons have not drunk wine to this very day because they obeyed their forefather's command. Carried out, baker, not forgotten.

Yes, baker. The prophets proclaimed, "Turn now, each of you, from your wicked ways, and correct your actions." (Jeremiah 35:15). God says He sent them again and again. And of the people He says, "…you have not inclined your ear or listened to Me."

Gods, baker, GODS! The prophets said, "Do not go after other gods to serve them." (Jeremiah 35:15). Notice the two actions in that warning: going after them and serving them. It comes in the same message as turning from wicked ways.
Kings is a fair guess, but the text says something else. The prophets said, "Do not go after other gods to serve them." (Jeremiah 35:15). The word is gods, and the warning is about serving them.

Disaster, baker. God says, "…I will bring to Judah and to all the residents of Jerusalem all the disaster I have pronounced against them…" (Jeremiah 35:17). It's a heavy line. He gives the reason too: "…I have spoken to them but they have not obeyed, and I have called to them but they have not answered."

Fields and vineyards aren't the promise here. The Rechabites say they have not owned vineyards or fields or crops (Jeremiah 35:9). The promise God gives is, "Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a man to stand before Me." (Jeremiah 35:19). It's about a man standing before God.

A throne would be a big promise, but it's not in the text. The LORD of Hosts says, "Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a man to stand before Me." (Jeremiah 35:19). The promise is about a man standing before God. Ruling Jerusalem isn't mentioned.
